zh: 嗯，但人类有一种判断力，有一种反馈能力，你知道的，智能体缺乏这个，而经典的授权语言也缺乏客户所寻找的、用于描述智能体需求的很多能力。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And so, for example, one of the things we did is we we recently launched Dogwood, which is this new policy language, happy to go into depth on that, but that is built as a specialized language for describing with mathematical certainty what an agent is allowed to do, what order it's allowed to do it in, whether it can do thing A after thing B, and so on.
zh: 所以，举例来说，我们做的一件事是，我们最近发布了 Dogwood，这是一种新的策略语言，很乐意深入讲讲，但它是作为一种专门语言构建的，用于以数学上的确定性来描述一个智能体被允许做什么、被允许按什么顺序做、它能否在做 B 之后做 A，等等。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And so it really all comes out from these customer needs and the fact that you know across the industry, people are saying, hey, agents are super exciting.
zh: 所以这真的全都来自这些客户需求，以及这样一个事实，你知道的，整个行业的人都在说，嘿，智能体超级令人兴奋。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: We're really excited about what we can do with agents.
zh: 我们对用智能体能做的事感到非常兴奋。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: We want to automate more, we want to serve our customers better, we want to spend our humans' time doing uh more important tasks.
zh: 我们想要更多自动化，我们想更好地服务我们的客户，我们想让我们的人类时间花在更重要 tasks 上。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And a key to doing that is having a great security story and a great policy story, uh a great isolation story, a great identity story.
zh: 而做到这一点的一个关键，是拥有一个出色的安全故事、出色的策略故事，出色的隔离故事、出色的身份故事。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Uh, and so we can build agents that we can trust to run autonomously and do critical things within our companies.
zh: 嗯，这样我们才能构建出我们可以信任其自主运行、并在公司内部做关键事情的智能体。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: And I was gonna mention autonomous actually, because that that I think that's the key.
zh: 我本来正想提到自主性，因为我认为那才是关键。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Uh in terms of being able to increase our trust and allow agents to run things more autonomously, we need them to essentially be able to make more decisions, to run longer processes, and they need that understanding uh or rather, they need that level of um those boundaries, those set deterministic boundaries without having to make their own decisions or do anything in a non-deterministic way.
zh: 嗯，在能够提升我们的信任、并允许智能体更自主地运行事情方面，我们需要它们本质上能够做更多决策、运行更长的流程，而它们需要那种理解，或者毋宁说，它们需要那种 um 那种边界、那些设定的确定性边界，而不必自己做决策或以任何非确定性的方式行事。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Uh they need those boundaries there whereby they can say, yes, you can you have access to this or you can do this, or no, this is you know beyond what we want to provide you with in this container or this space.
zh: 嗯，它们需要那些边界在那里，凭此它们可以说，是的，你可以，你有权限访问这个或者你可以做这个，或者不，这你知道的超出了我们在这一容器或这个空间里想提供给你的范围。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Um I think that's you know so important, and I think the last month or so has actually shown how important that is in terms of um in terms of that belief and trust.
zh: 嗯我认为这你知道的非常重要，而且我认为过去一个月左右实际上已经展示了这有多重要，就 um 就那种信念和信任而言。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Um and and as we go forward with autonomy and interfactories and long-running processes, how do you see people using this kind of a tool to to run their containers?
zh: 嗯，随着我们在自主性、interfactories 和长时间运行流程上前进，你如何看待人们使用这样一种工具来运行他们的容器?

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Do you see like configurations that people will essentially be assigning on various tasks?
zh: 你是否预见人们基本上会在各种任务上指定的一些配置?

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Um how would someone set this up?
zh: 嗯，有人会如何做这样的设置?

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Well, one of the things that we know from you know decades of research into psychology and operations and operators is that humans are really bad supervisors.
zh: 好吧，我们从你几十年来对心理学、运营和操作员的研究中所知道的一件事是，人类是非常糟糕的监督者。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Uh you know, just really bad at watching things go by and pushing the red button when something bad happens.
zh: 嗯你知道的，真的很不擅长盯着东西过去看，并在坏事发生时按下红色按钮。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Um and you know, there are multiple dynamics behind that.
zh: 嗯，你知道的，这背后有多种动态。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: You know, one of them is this classic research from the 80s, there's this great paper called Um The Ironies of Automation about how as an you know a system becomes better and better and better, uh the failure modes become weirder and less frequent and becomes much harder for the human supervisor to understand when they happen, recognize them and react correctly to them.
zh: 你知道的，其一是上世纪 80 年代的这项经典研究，有一篇很棒的论文叫 Um The Ironies of Automation，讲的是随着一个你知道的系统变得越来越好越来越好，其失效模式会变得越来越怪异、越来越罕见，而人类监督者要理解它们何时发生、识别它们并对它们做出正确反应就变得困难得多。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And so I think the only solution to this is that autonomy, right?
zh: 所以我认为唯一的解决方案就是自主性，对吧?

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Pull the human out of the loop, make them not watch the loop go round and push the button when something bad happens.
zh: 把人类从回路中拉出来，让他们不用看着回路转圈、在坏事发生时按下按钮。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Certainly not make them say yes, yes, yes, after every code generation task, because you know who's gonna do that?
zh: 当然更不要让他们在每个代码生成任务之后都说，是、是、是，因为你知道谁会去做那个?

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Um, but instead pop the human out and say, let's start by describing what good looks like.
zh: 嗯，而是把人类弹出去，然后说，让我们从描述什么是好的开始。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Let's start by describing the set of things that you would like the system to do.
zh: 让我们从描述你希望系统去做的那组事情开始。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Um, and then once we have that description, we will apply it to the agent without requiring a human to go around and do those things.
zh: 嗯，然后一旦我们有了那个描述，我们就会把它应用于智能体，而不需要一个人四处去亲手做那些事情。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And so how do you do that?
zh: 那么你怎么做到这一点?

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Well, some of that is encoding of it's encoding of common sense, right?
zh: 好吧，其中一部分是对 um 它是对常识的编码，对吧?

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: You know as you develop a piece of code, um, you know, what kinds of interactions it should have with the system, right?
zh: 你知道的，当你开发一段代码时，um 你知道的，它应该与系统发生哪几种交互，对吧?

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: It's gonna do, you know, get pull and get push, but only in the the um the repository it's working in, right?
zh: 它会去做，你知道的，get pull 和 get push，但只在其正在工作的 um 那个仓库里，对吧?

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: If it goes and tries to do a get push to a different project, well, that's probably bad.
zh: 如果它跑去对一个不同的项目做 get push，嗯，那多半是坏的。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And so we're going to encode that little piece of common sense into a policy.
zh: 所以我们要把这一小块常识编码进一个策略。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Um and part of that is writing that kind of library of those common sense policies.
zh: 嗯，其中一部分是编写那种由这些常识策略组成的库。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Part of that is this process of natural language to policy where you can say, um, you know, this can read anything on my hard drive except the stuff in my secret documents folder, and and have that automatically and reliably turned into a policy.
zh: 其中一部分是自然语言到策略的过程，你可以说，um 你知道的，这可以读取我硬盘上的任何东西，除了我机密文档文件夹里的东西，并且让那被自动且可靠地转成一个策略。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And then part of that is going out over a company and discovering all of the policies and practices and so on and encoding those existing practices into policy.
zh: 然后其中一部分是走遍一家公司，发现所有的策略和实践等等，并把那些现有实践编码进策略。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Um so to answer your direct question, I think the minority case is people writing policy directly.
zh: 嗯，所以直接回答你的问题，我认为少数情况是人们直接编写策略。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: I think there are going to be some people writing dogwood or CEDA or OPA or whatever policy language they're using.
zh: 我认为会有一些人编写 dogwood 或 CEDA 或 OPA 或他们使用的任何策略语言。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: But the vast majority aren't going to engage at that level and don't want to because those languages are quite specialized and fairly difficult to learn, um, but instead are going to be engaging at that natural language level of saying, you know, here's what here's what good looks like.
zh: 但绝大多数人不会在那个层面参与，也不想那样，因为那些语言相当专门化且相当难学，um 相反，他们会在那个自然语言层面参与，说，你知道的，这就是这就是好的样子。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: There could be me as a developer saying, here's what good looks like for me as a person, or it could be, you know, somebody in the CISO's office saying, you know, here's what good looks like for us as an organization, here's our standard and policy for handling customer content, and our standard and policy for handling our code, and then encoding those.
zh: 可以是我作为一名开发者说，这是对我个人而言好的样子，或者可以是，你知道的，CISO 办公室里的某个人说，你知道的，这是对我们作为组织而言好的样子，这是我们处理客户内容的标准和策略，以及我们处理我们代码的标准和策略，然后把它们编码起来。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And often all of those things will come together.
zh: 而且常常是所有这些东西会一起到来。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And so I'll have some things from my CISO's office, I'll probably have some things from Legal, I'll have some things from myself as a developer, and all of those go together and provide this shell around my agent where we can strongly and deterministically make sure that the agent is following all of those policies by using one of these lower level languages.
zh: 所以我会有一些来自我 CISO 办公室的东西，我大概会有一些来自法务的东西，我会有一些来自我自己作为开发者的东西，所有这些合在一起，为我的智能体提供这层外壳，让我们可以通过使用其中一种更低层的语言，强有力且确定性地确保智能体遵循所有那些策略。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: I I was gonna ask actually whether whether you see this as something uh in your experience that is an organizational level or a department level, uh from legal, from security.
zh: 我我本来正想问，实际上，是否你在你的经验中把这看作是组织层面的还是部门层面的，uh 来自法务、来自安全。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Is it is it majority from those from those teams down to developers, or is it a is it you know closer to a 50-50?
zh: 它是它是 majority 来自那些团队、向下传导到开发者，还是说它你知道的更接近于 50-50?

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Um I think it's closer to a 50-50.
zh: 嗯，我认为更接近于 50-50。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Like there is some things that my security teams deeply care about, right?
zh: 比如说，有一些东西是我的安全团队深切关心的，对吧?

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: The way that customer content is is handled and where it is allowed to be in a system, for example.
zh: 客户内容被处理的方式，以及它被允许处于系统中的什么位置，例如。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And I want every developer in the company's agents to be held to maintaining that standard.
zh: 而我希望公司里每个开发者的智能体都被要求维持那个标准。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And then there's some things that my security teams don't care about, right?
zh: 然后还有一些我的安全团队不关心的东西，对吧?

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Like, can my development agent delete documents from my documents folder?
zh: 比如，我的开发智能体能不能从我文档文件夹里删除文档?

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Well, my security teams don't really care about that because there's no, you know, there's no customer impact of that, there's no organizational impact of that.
zh: 嗯，我的安全团队其实并不关心那个，因为没有，你知道，那没有客户影响，没有组织影响。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: But as an end user, I care about that super deeply.
zh: 但作为最终用户，我非常非常在意那个。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: I don't want that stuff deleted.
zh: 我不想要那些东西被删掉。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And so I'm going to, it's going to be a mix of these things.
zh: 所以我会，这会是这些东西的混合体。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Um and, you know, especially as we get down to individual developers, we know that across the industry, and and and certainly, you know, even within teams and within organizations, development practices vary.
zh: 嗯，而且，你知道，尤其是当我们下沉到个体开发者时，我们知道在整个行业里，当然，你知道，甚至在团队内部和组织内部，开发实践各不相同。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: There's a wide range of what normal looks like.
zh: 「正常」是什么样子有很大的范围。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: There's a wide range of tools that people use.
zh: 人们使用的工具有很大的范围。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And so just like you know, most big software organizations don't try and push down a, you will use exactly these tools at this time type software engineering practice, they're not going to succeed at pushing down a complete end-to-end, this is your agent policy, because that needs to be adapted to the kinds of development you're doing.
zh: 所以就像，你知道，大多数大型软件组织不会试图强行推行一种「你必须在这个时间使用这些工具」式的软件工程实践一样，它们也不会成功地强行推行一套完整的端到端的「这是你的智能体政策」，因为这需要适应你正在做的开发类型。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And even day-to-day, right?
zh: 而且甚至每天都不一样，对吧？

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Like sometimes I'm writing back-end Rust code and I want to set a certain kind of standard, and I want to write things like, hey, you aren't allowed to commit before Clippy is happy with this code.
zh: 比如，有时我在写后端 Rust 代码，我想设定某种标准，我想写上类似的话：嘿，在 Clippy 对这段代码满意之前，你不允许提交。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And sometimes I'm writing, you know, a quick and dirty prototype of a, you know, of a of a web demo.
zh: 而有时我在写，你知道，一个 web 演示的，你知道，一个快速粗糙的原型。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And I don't want to set any of those standards.
zh: 而且我不想设定任何这些标准。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And I'm just like, okay, we'll just hack this thing together with whatever tools make sense, because we're going to show it off for 15 minutes and then discard it.
zh: 我就是，好吧，我们就用任何合理的工具把这个东西凑出来，因为我们只会展示它 15 分钟，然后就扔掉。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And so I'm going to have different policies.
zh: 所以我会有不同的政策。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And so those policies do have to come from different places and be dynamic and be contextual.
zh: 所以这些政策确实必须来自不同的地方，并且是动态的、情境化的。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Hey everyone, hope you're enjoying the episode so far.
zh: 嘿，各位，希望你们到目前为止喜欢这期节目。

speaker: Simon Maple

en: But for whatever reason, many of you have yet to subscribe to the channel.

speaker: Simon Maple

speaker: Simon Maple
en: It really does make a difference and lets us continue to improve the quality of our guests and build an even better product for you.
zh: 这确实很重要，能让我们继续提升嘉宾的质量，为你打造更好的产品。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Alright, back to the episode.
zh: 好了，回到节目。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: I want to go to another piece that you wrote about, which is the agentic software development hypothesis.
zh: 我想谈谈你写的另一篇文章，是关于智能体软件开发假说的。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: And you also mention um uh uh a a number of different kind of like forms of this, which is the weak form, strong form, and strongest form.
zh: 而且你还提到了，嗯，呃，呃，它的若干不同形式，也就是弱形式、强形式和最强形式。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Um I'd love you to walk us through the agentic software development hypothesis first, then we can kind of cover the rest.
zh: 嗯，我希望你先带我们走一遍智能体软件开发假说，然后我们再谈剩下的部分。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Yeah, you might have to remind me exactly what I wrote in that post.
zh: 好的，你可能得提醒我那篇文章里到底写了什么。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Um but it essentially it comes down to this idea that the hard part of software building is um I'm gonna say specification building.
zh: 嗯，但它本质上是归结为这样一个想法：软件构建中难的部分是，嗯，我要说是规格构建。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And and and what that means is describing what you want.
zh: 而这意味着的是描述你想要什么。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Um and it describing what you want in sufficient detail that it is, let's say, a complete description of what you want.
zh: 嗯，用足够详细的方式描述你想要的东西，可以说是对你所想要的东西的完整描述。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Once you have that specification, once you have that what you want written down, my belief is that we're going to see the building and maintenance of reliable, efficient implementations of that software become over time entirely automated.
zh: 一旦你有了那个规格，一旦你把想要的东西写下来，我的信念是，我们会看到该软件的可靠、高效实现的构建和维护，随着时间推移变得完全自动化。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Um we're gonna see that first, and I think we've already seen that with, let's say, these closed specifications.
zh: 嗯，我们会先看到这一点，而且我认为我们已经通过，比如说，这些封闭规格看到了这一点。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Hey, I want something that implements this type of file format, and it's very well described.
zh: 嘿，我想要一个实现这种文件格式的东西，而且它被描述得非常清楚。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Um, and and and we've already seen that.
zh: 嗯，我们已经看到了。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: And we're gonna see that grow to larger and larger systems, systems with more UI, systems with more complex interactions.
zh: 而且我们会看到它扩展到越来越大的系统，有更多 UI 的系统，有更复杂交互的系统。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: But I think over time, all of that kind of specification down of software development is going to become automated and driven by an automation loop.
zh: 但我认为，随着时间推移，所有这类软件开发规格的下沉都会变得自动化，并由一个自动化循环驱动。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Um and you know, the the the kind of stronger claim is that the vast majority of software can be specified crisply enough to enable that kind of automation?
zh: 嗯，你知道，更强的主张是，绝大多数软件都可以被足够清晰地规格化，从而实现那种自动化吗？

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Yeah, absolutely.
zh: 是的，绝对可以。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Now, in that same post, you mentioned that very few tasks have complete specifications, and you also talked about oracles that can be deterministic.
zh: 现在，在同一篇文章里，你提到很少有任务拥有完整的规格，你还谈到了可以是确定性的 oracle。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Um, and you mentioned oracles aren't deterministic.
zh: 嗯，而你提到 oracle 不是确定性的。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: So I wonder, are we relocating the the the tough piece of the problem uh to be in identifying an oracle that's deterministic or being able to create that complete specification?
zh: 所以我想知道，我们是不是把问题中难的部分迁移到了识别一个确定性的 oracle、或者能够创建那个完整规格上？

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Is that still more of a human issue?
zh: 那这仍然是更多是人类的问题吗？

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: Yeah, for sure.
zh: 是的，当然是。

speaker: Marc Brooker
en: I think that is where the you know where where a huge amount of the human the human work comes in is is creating those oracles, creating those specifications.
zh: 我认为那就是，你知道，大量人类工作所在之处，就是创建那些 oracle，创建那些规格。
